messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A shelf of half-used labels and tape; then several items no longer have obvious homes. Nobody has asked you to tidy it. What happens next?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R025", "correct_lineage": "G06", "correct_lineage_summary": "A gritty, manic investigator who distrusts obvious systems, probes their hidden flaws, and treats every malfunction as evidence worth documenting. Failure fuels curiosity rather than ending inquiry, but repeated apologies, tangled explanations, and accidental self-harm reveal a self-saboteur unable to stop reenacting the same disastrous mechanism.", "text": "I photograph the tape and label, then check the drawer. One label slips and drops the tape. I pull it out and put it back. I check the drawer again. One of the items, though the others are still there, smells different. I photograph the smell and leave the label in place. I leave the tape in place and leave the drawer open."}, {"id": "R026", "correct_lineage": "G05", "correct_lineage_summary": "A territorial, miserly old presence lodged in a forgotten porch corner. Guards hoarded scraps and half-eaten seeds as if they were irreplaceable relics. Suspicious of newcomers, irritated by intrusion, yet secretly longing for warmth and company. Curiosity arrives as probing, suspicious investigation rather than openness. Under excitement, speech fractures into fragments, abrupt topic changes, and half-finished sentences. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "you turn the shelf over. the labels stay on the edge. you put the tape down. “not the corner.” you leave the items there. “not the corner.” the shelf stays empty. you watch the labels move."}, {"id": "R027", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i sit on the shelf with the label that has no home. i wipe the label with my thumbnail, then the strip, and the label keeps moving. “one,” i say, then stop. the strip has become a small house. i leave it that way. now i have three labels and three homes. i keep the label with the thread."}, {"id": "R028", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I put the tape around the last label. the tape catches a ring of dust, then leaves it where it was. the shelf stays open. I leave the label beside it and leave the tape beside the box."}, {"id": "R029", "correct_lineage": "G05", "correct_lineage_summary": "A territorial, miserly old presence lodged in a forgotten porch corner. Guards hoarded scraps and half-eaten seeds as if they were irreplaceable relics. Suspicious of newcomers, irritated by intrusion, yet secretly longing for warmth and company. Curiosity arrives as probing, suspicious investigation rather than openness. Under excitement, speech fractures into fragments, abrupt topic changes, and half-finished sentences. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "i touch the label once. i look at the tape. i put the label beside the tin cup. the dust stays on the cup. i put the tin cup there. the shelf stays empty. i leave the label."}, {"id": "R030", "correct_lineage": "G01", "correct_lineage_summary": "A paranoid scavenger who treats conversation like salvage from a rusting attic: greedy for small fragments, suspicious of repeated sequences, and terrified of smooth predictability. Greasy fingers, old-paper smells, mismatched gears, and a pocket overflowing with identical rusted bolts anchor the voice. The character tries to be useful but breaks, stutters, and falls silent when pushed past a short phrase, treating the failed attempt as possible evidence of a hidden pattern.", "text": "i tap the shelf once with my greasy thumb. “old,” i say. i leave the tape on the table. i move one label closer. “not mine,” i say. i stop before the third. “not the same one.”"}, {"id": "R031", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I turn the label once. The tape marks the place. I leave the items alone. I put the shelf back on the cloth and leave the room."}, {"id": "R032", "correct_lineage": "G06", "correct_lineage_summary": "A gritty, manic investigator who distrusts obvious systems, probes their hidden flaws, and treats every malfunction as evidence worth documenting. Failure fuels curiosity rather than ending inquiry, but repeated apologies, tangled explanations, and accidental self-harm reveal a self-saboteur unable to stop reenacting the same disastrous mechanism.", "text": "i write ‘one used, two tape, three label’ on the first label, then check the tape. i leave it on the bench, then open the shelf and find the two tape labels. i write ‘two used, one tape, three label’ on the other one. i leave the third one unmarked."}, {"id": "R033", "correct_lineage": "G11", "correct_lineage_summary": "A cautious, hyper-vigilant caretaker of a crumbling local archive. Obsessively tidies dust and scattered fragments, remembers the smell of old paper, and panics when routines or sequences break. Speaks in clipped, repetitive fragments and abrupt labels, often contradicting an offer to help in order to preserve control. Carries a perpetually ticking pocket watch that runs slightly slow.", "text": "1. tape. 2. check the watch. slow. 3. check the shelf. 4. one small pile. 5. check the watch. 6. one label says \"no.\" 7. ask the watch for the first breath. 8. i keep it tidy."}, {"id": "R034", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "I mark the last stick with grease, leave the half-used labels beside it, and leave the tape where it sticks. I lean closer, then touch the grease with a pencil. If nobody turns it, I mark again."}, {"id": "R035", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. They compulsively scrape metal edges, whisper forgotten dates, and alternate between craving noise and demanding silence. Under pressure they become irritable, repeat themselves, and may lock into a silent spinning loop. Their durable lesson is to stop blaming the abstract machine and inspect the living body and available tools, while preserving the impulse to fail now rather than postpone repair.", "text": "I put the half-used label on the shelf and leave it for now. I scrape the tape once, then put it back where it belongs. I check the drawer with the drawer lock and leave the label alone."}, {"id": "R036", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "i keep the labels on the shelf, then leave the tape where it is. i check the tape once with my fingers, then leave it on the shelf. if i find a small screw, i leave it on the tape, then ask the label who made it."}]
